text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Wednesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Lithuania's election observer in Chechnya, MP Algirdas Endriukaitis, refused to participate in the OSCE mission's work and do his duty. Such casts a shadow on the credibility of Lithuania, said a high-ranking foreign ministry official.
- Parliament budget and finance comittee head Elvyra Kuneviciene says former finance minister Rolandas Matiliauskas, who quit over a bank-loan scandal last week, was not guilty.
- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas would like Arturas Paulauskas, deputy prosecutor general, to take the post of prosecutor general.

- Vilfima brokerage topped the list of the most active players on the Lithuanian market. Its share capital is 2.5 million litas and turnover in equities trade 54 million litas. Vilfima is followed by Vilnius Bank and Suprema.
- Birziu Naftotiekis had 41.7 million litas profit in 1996, 4 percent less than in 1995 when it was 43.4 million litas.

- The head of the state security department confirms to Brazauskas that Juras Abromavicius, killed in a car blasts on Friday, might have lost his life because of information known to him as an employee of the special services.
- Lithuanian PM Gediminas Vagnorius will vist Stockholm on Monday to meet Swedish counterpart Goran Persson to discuss European integration.

- It is not enough to talk about open doors to NATO, Lithuania would like to be mentioned among the firt countries to be accepted to the allience, Foreign Minister Algirdas Saudargas said in Copenhagen.
- EU PHARE transport expert Alain Storose, 49, was found dead in his apartment on Monday. Foul play is not suspected.
- The ruling Homeland Union party will not compromise over the post of the prosecutor general.
